# KnowYourCG 2 (binary: kycg) — agent reference
# Canonical: https://zhou-lab.github.io/kycg/llms.txt
# Human guide: https://zhou-lab.github.io/kycg/
# Source: https://github.com/zhou-lab/kycg
# For exact flags, always run: kycg <command> -h

## What it is

KnowYourCG 2 is the C implementation of KnowYourCG: functional enrichment
analysis of DNA methylation at CpG resolution, with YAME as the computational
backend. The binary is `kycg`. It scales to whole-genome row spaces (29M CpGs)
as well as arrays. The Bioconductor R package is KnowYourCG v1 and continues
on the 1.x series; the two are parallel implementations, not an upgrade path,
and their statistics agree to floating-point tolerance.

Cite: Goldberg et al. KnowYourCG. Sci Adv 2025;11(43):eadw3027.
doi:10.1126/sciadv.adw3027

## Install

  conda install -c zhou-lab -c conda-forge kycg yame

Install `yame` alongside kycg. kycg links libyame statically, so the backend
library is inside the binary, but the `yame` COMMAND is a separate package and
the documented row-space check (`yame info query.cg kb.cm`) needs it. kycg has
no `info` subcommand of its own.

Knowledgebases are NOT in the package — `kycg fetch` pulls them on demand. The
binary carries only the registry of tags and digests it can verify.

Source build (YAME is a submodule; `make` drives its `make lib`):

  git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/zhou-lab/kycg
  cd kycg && make            # make CURL=0 builds without fetch
  make yame-bin              # the yame COMMAND (make alone builds only libyame)

Dependencies are YAME's: vendored htslib, zlib, libm, pthreads, librt. libcurl is
optional and used only by `kycg fetch`. `kycg --version` (alias `-v`) prints
the build, the YAME it links, the store, the registry tag it can verify, and
whether curl is in. `-h`/`--help` (all levels) exit 0.

## Commands

  kycg fetch      browse/download knowledgebases into the verified store
  kycg test       set enrichment: query vs knowledgebases -> TSV
  kycg annotate   label a table of probe IDs with the sets they fall in

File inspection is `yame info` (kycg builds on YAME's .cx formats). Plotting is
cinderplot, as a separate process — kycg emits TSV and nothing more.

## fetch — the knowledgebase store

  kycg fetch                    # browse everything (full-screen tree)
  kycg fetch hg38               # open with hg38 checked; f starts the download
  kycg fetch hg38:CGI,ChromHMM  # open with just those checked
  kycg fetch -f hg38            # download now: no browser, no questions
  kycg fetch | grep -v '^#'     # TSV catalogue, for scripts

  -d DIR  store directory [$YAME_DATA_HOME, else the shared store]
  -o SETS comma-separated subset by set name
  -f      download now, no browser
  -r      re-download even what is present and verified

Ten collections: `hg38` (32 sets), `mm10` (28) and `mm39` (1) from
KYCGKB_<genome>, plus MSA, EPICv2, EPIC, HM450, HM27, MM285, Mammal40 from
InfiniumAnnotation. Fetched sets are ordinary files — a path works anywhere a
set name does.

Browser keys: arrows or j/k move, `→`/`←` unfold/fold a target, space checks a
set, `i` toggles the description pane, `f` fetches, `d` changes store, `t`
tests (in `test`), `q` quits. Sets already present show ✓ and cannot be checked.

Trust model: EVERY FILE CARRIES ITS OWN DIGEST in src/registry.h, and a
download is verified against that, never against a fetched manifest. Downloads
land on a `.part` sibling and are renamed only after the digest matches. kycg
then writes a SHA256SUMS derived from the same rows, so the store re-verifies
with `sha256sum -c` and no kycg code. A set upstream with no row in the
registry cannot be verified, so it is not offered. The digest is checked again
when a file is READ: a copy this build does not pin warns and the command
proceeds; a file that is absent is an error naming the `kycg fetch` that gets
it.

## test — set enrichment

  kycg test -m mm10:CGI            query.cg > results.tsv
  kycg test -m mm10:CGI,ChromHMM   query.cg
  kycg test -m mm10                query.cg   # everything cached for mm10
  kycg test -m path/to/some.cm     query.cg   # a path is taken literally

  -m SPEC  path or target[:sets]; repeatable [required]
  -a STR   alternative: greater|less|two.sided [greater]
  -c       continuous query: set enrichment score, as GSEA
  -G       correct FDR globally instead of within knowledgebase
  -s FILE  sample names for the query
  -M       load the knowledgebase into memory
  -F       full file paths instead of basenames
  -H       suppress the header line
  -o FILE  write to FILE instead of stdout

Per (query sample, knowledgebase record): the four contingency counts, a
one-sided hypergeometric tail in log10, six effect sizes, and BH-corrected FDR.
Columns:

  query_file query db_file db group nU nQ nD overlap
  estimate log10_p p_value fdr neglog10_fdr
  cf_jaccard cf_mcc cf_overlap cf_npmi cf_dice
  beta depth

The first nine are `yame summary`'s columns renamed; the rest kycg adds.
`estimate` is Log2OddsRatio at full precision.

`-c` takes a continuous query instead: one value per row, format 3 (scored
as beta, uncovered rows missing) or format 4 (negative is missing). Each set
is scored by a GSEA-style running sum over the rows sorted by value, as
knowYourCG's testEnrichmentSEA does. `estimate` is the enrichment score in
[-1, 1]: positive when the set crowds the LARGE values, negative when it
crowds the small ones (knowYourCG >= 1.9.3; 1.8.x had the opposite sign).
`log10_p` comes from 1000 permutations, both tails pooled into one null so
negating the query never changes it, with a fitted normal past the last
draw. The null is seeded from (rows, set size): reruns are identical. The
row has the same columns; nU = nQ = rows with a value, overlap = the set's
rows with a value, beta = their mean value, cf_* = NA. -a does not apply.

  kycg test -c -m mm10:ChromHMM beta.cg

Pool knowledgebases into ONE invocation: `-m mm10` against 30 sets decompresses
the query once, 30 processes decompress it 30 times.

## annotate — label probe IDs

  kycg annotate -m EPIC:CGI,ProbeType hits.tsv > annotated.tsv

  -m SPEC  path or platform[:sets]; repeatable [required]
  -p PLAT  platform, when -m is a plain path
  -c COL   probe ID column: name or 1-based index [Probe_ID, else 1]
  -i       indicator columns (0/1) per set, for modelling
  -s SEP   separator when a probe is in several sets [,]
  -H       input has no header line
  -o FILE  write to FILE instead of stdout

Keeps every column and row in order and appends one column per knowledgebase.
Arrays only, and the platform is NAMED rather than inferred — a wrong guess
would produce a full table of confident, wrong answers.

## Traps

- `p_value` and `fdr` read 0 for any strong result: they are 10^log10_p, which
  underflows around log10_p = -308 while real enrichments run past -1500. Sort,
  threshold and plot on `log10_p` / `neglog10_fdr`, which stay in log space.
- FDR is corrected within one query sample and one knowledgebase (the family
  knowYourCG's testEnrichment corrects over). Adding samples or knowledgebases
  to one invocation does not change any FDR already reported. `-G` widens the
  stratum to all knowledgebases (matching mtc_by_group=FALSE); the `group`
  column then reads `(global)` instead of a file name.
- Everything is POSITIONAL: a `.cg` and a `.cm` are comparable only if row i is
  the same CpG in both. kycg asserts equal row counts and fails loudly, but it
  cannot detect two files that share a row count from different row spaces —
  keeping them matched is the user's job.
- kycg never infers a platform and never prompts off a TTY: a redirected stdout
  makes `fetch` write plain TSV, a named target download without asking, and a
  missing `-m` an error rather than a wait.
- `estimate` (= log2 odds ratio) is not always finite. Zero overlap makes the
  odds ratio 0, and log2 clamps to a sentinel near -1022 (log2 of DBL_MIN);
  infinite odds ratio lands near +1024 (log2 of DBL_MAX). On a whole-genome
  query most sets have no overlap, so most rows carry the sentinel — filter
  `abs(estimate) < 1000` (or a tighter bound) before plotting `estimate`, as
  KYCG_plotVolcano does.
- Downloading happens in `fetch` and nowhere else.
- Tags are per file, so there is no global tag to override; `-t` is gone.

## Registry — a build is coupled to a data generation

Per-file URLs, digests, sizes and row counts are compiled into
`src/registry.h`, projected from YAME's shared table by kycg's own emitter.
Following an upstream tag:

  make registry && make        # regenerates src/registry.h and src/kbinfo.h
  tools/check_dimensions.sh        # confirm pinned row counts still hold (needs yame)

The trade is reproducibility for immediacy: a kycg release means an exact,
known set of knowledgebases.

## Knowledgebases

What `kycg fetch` offers, grouped by the KnowYourCG paper's four
categories: each knowledgebase, then the builds and platforms that
carry it with their number of sets (records or states in the .cm).
Set names and sizes are on the page's Knowledgebases tab.

### Sequence features
- G4peaksHighConfidence (G-quadruplexes): MSA 2
- GCfrac (GC fraction): mm10 140
- kmer10 (10-mer context): mm10 32,897
- nFlankCG (Flanking CpG density): hg38 46, mm10 43, MSA 31, EPICv2 37, EPIC
  35, HM450 34, HM27 32, MM285 32, Mammal40 31
- nFlankCG100 (Flanking CpG density, 100 bp): hg38 32, mm10 30
- nFlankCG50 (Flanking CpG density, 50 bp): hg38 18, mm10 19
- Tetranuc2 (Tetranucleotide context): hg38 4, mm10 4, MSA 4, EPICv2 4, EPIC
  4, HM450 4, HM27 4, MM285 4, Mammal40 4
- Tetranuc4 (Tetranucleotide context, uncollapsed): mm10 11, MM285 11

### Genomic features

- TFBS (Transcription factor binding sites): hg38 1,359, mm10 703
- TFBSFreq (TFBS density): mm10 7

- Win100k (100 kb windows): hg38 29,511, mm10 26,604
- Win1m (1 Mb windows): mm10 2,673
- Win30k (30 kb windows): mm10 88,442

## Correctness

`make test` checks the hypergeometric tail and BH against R's `phyper()` /
`p.adjust()` across small, array-scale, whole-genome and deep-tail regimes
(worst relative error 2.6e-16). `tests/validate_vs_R.R` re-derives every column
of a real run with the same calls knowYourCG makes. `tests/validate_sea_vs_R.R`
runs `-c` and testEnrichmentSEA on the same data: estimates agree to 4e-11,
p-values in rank (R permutes 100 times, kycg 1000). The tail uses Loader's
saddle-point expansion (as R's `dhyper()` does); BH is applied in log space,
since a linear-space BH would assign FDR 0 to every underflowed row.

## Layout

  src/hypergeo.{c,h}  log-space hypergeometric tail + BH (pure, no YAME)
  src/enrich.{c,h}    effect sizes, FDR strata, TSV emission
  src/store.{c,h}     store paths and enumeration
  src/registry.h      generated: per-file urls, digests, sizes, row counts
  src/kbinfo.h        generated from data/knowledgebases.tsv
  src/ui.{c,h}        terminal layer: tree browser, panels, TTY gating
  src/fetch.c src/test.c src/main.c
  tools/              generators for registry.h and kbinfo.h
  external/YAME/      submodule

`src/registry.h` and `src/kbinfo.h` are generated — edit the catalog/data
inputs and regenerate; do not hand-edit them.
